views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep existing tariffs in place, leave the December 15 List 4B hike as unused leverage, and drive the October 11 Phase One understanding onto paper without new unilateral concessions. Do not raise rates again while talks are live, and do not roll back Lists 1–3 or delist Huawei to buy a handshake. Lock specific, dated agricultural purchase volumes, a currency chapter, and enforceable IP/copyright language; treat Phase Two structural issues as sequential, not as a reason to blow up the ceasefire.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is real but contained, not existential. The dispute is already biting US interests: ISM manufacturing fell to 47.8 in September (lowest since June 2009), with ISM citing global trade and a contraction in new export orders from July; US farm exports to China fell from about $24B in 2017 to roughly $9.2B over the prior twelve months; the Fed has cut (effective funds 2.38% in June to 1.83% in October) and the 10-year yield dropped from 2.51% on May 6 to a late-August low of 1.47% during the List 4 / CNY-7 / manipulator shock, recovering only to 1.78% by October 30 after the Phase One pause. That is material sectoral damage and political pressure in the farm belt, but it is not a supply-chain or recession-level threat to the US as a whole—services still expanded, and the October 15 hike of List 3 from 25% to 30% was suspended. The reading is therefore above neutral (+0.25), not at the +0.5 “high” anchor. Action should be negotiate, not escalate or concede. Escalation now would likely kill a live text process (USTR said on October 25 the sides were “close to finalizing some sections” after the Lighthizer–Mnuchin–Liu He call) and would land Dec 15 consumer tariffs (phones, laptops, toys) on US households. Concession is premature: China has not confirmed Trump’s $40–50B annual farm figure (Beijing and later reporting pointed nearer $20B in year one, demand- and price-contingent, and tied to US tariff relief); Huawei remains off the table; May 2019 showed a near-complete text can be walked back. Hold the $250B at 25% and List 4A at 15%, paper Phase One, and keep Dec 15 as the bargaining chip rather than firing it or giving it away.
key_factors: Phase One announced Oct 11 but still unwritten; Dec 15 List 4B still undecided
US manufacturing contraction (ISM 47.8) and crushed farm exports to China
China slowdown (Q3 GDP 6.0%) increases Beijing's incentive to deal, but purchase numbers are disputed
May 2019 collapse is the relevant precedent against premature concessions
Huawei Entity List and structural IP/tech-transfer left for later phases
Fed easing and the Aug–Sep Treasury rally show markets pricing growth/trade risk, not US collapse

sources_cited.excerpt: After Washington talks, Trump announces a "Phase One" deal in principle: China to buy roughly $40–50B of US agricultural products annually; IP and currency issues also cited. Planned mid-October tariff hike delayed.

Trump tweets that negotiations are going "too slowly" and that China is attempting to "renegotiate." Orders List 3 raised from 10% to 25% on May 10 and directs preparation of tariffs on remaining Chinese imports (~$300B).
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
List 4A takes effect at 15% (~$110–125B of Chinese imports). China's first tranche of the ~$75B retaliation also takes effect.
Federal funds effective rate fell from 2.38% (June 2019) to 1.83% (October 2019), a 55bp / ~23% decline over the window.
10-year Treasury yield fell from 2.51% on 2019-05-06 to 1.47% on 2019-08-28 during the August escalation, then recovered to 1.78% on 2019-10-30 after the Phase One pause.
ISM manufacturing index dropped to 47.8 in September, lowest since June 2009; ISM chair said global trade remains the most significant issue, with new export orders contracting since July.
Phase One covers agriculture, currency and some IP; takes up to five weeks to write; Lighthizer said no decision on December tariffs; Huawei not part of the deal.
USTR: after the Oct 25 Lighthizer–Mnuchin–Liu He call, the two sides 'made headway on specific issues and are close to finalizing some sections of the agreement.'
China willing to buy as much as $20B of US farm goods in year one if Phase One is signed—restoring roughly pre-war levels—not the $40–50B Trump cited as an immediate annual run-rate.
China Q3 GDP +6.0% y/y, below forecast, slowest in decades; September industrial output +5.8% after a weak August.
